A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PROSE and ManyPeptidesMD. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across the extensive appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular simulations, model evaluations, architectural ablations, sampling comparisons, and temperature-transfer experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons, dataset-scaling experiments, further ablations, and sequence-length extrapolation results.

M1.justification: V2 Appendix E.3 introduces an L2 penalty between current-model and pretrained-teacher log densities into the stated fine-tuning procedure, beyond v1 D.3's resampling and likelihood training. The overall flow and sampling framework remains. The abstract's change from 280M to 285M parameters does not establish resizing: v1 Table 8 already reports 285M.

E1.justification: The ManyPeptidesMD training corpus and existing peptide-length coverage remain. V2 Appendix F.5 adds YQNPDGSQA, a nine-residue peptide, and ten-residue Chignolin, explicitly testing extrapolation beyond the eight-residue training maximum. This introduces a substantive generalization scenario absent from v1.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds evaluated TimeWarp, BioEmu, and UniSim baselines alongside the retained flow comparators; Table 4 additionally introduces TimeWarp into the larger-budget sampling comparison. Conversely, Figure 1 removes the equivariant-flow comparison curve and focuses on molecular dynamics versus PROSE.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes ablation training from peptides through length four to the full training range, and increases the sampling budget from 25,000 to 200,000. The MD benchmark changes from 1 ns to 1 microsecond with revised frame sampling and reweighting. The stated TICA inputs change from the heavy-atom subspace to pairwise distances and dihedrals; v2 also introduces clustering-based JSD evaluation. These changes limit direct comparison of updated scores.

E4.justification: V2 replaces the short-peptide additive ablations with full-range component-removal tests. Appendix F expands the previously described parameter-matching analysis with numerical results and adds look-ahead-conditioning ablation, training-data scaling, and beyond-training-length tests. The temperature and mode-coverage case studies also change from SAEL to RLMM.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The note about unique seeds for parallel ECNF++ sampling remains. Newly reported ESS per second is an efficiency metric, not a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Retained tables contain revised values: for example, PROSE's tetrapeptide E-W2 changes from 0.877 to 0.932 in Table 2. The octopeptide TICA ranking against TarFlow reverses under the revised feature specification, so this is not an established same-setting gain. V2 adds extensive baseline, ablation, scaling, JSD, extrapolation, and efficiency results. Its replacement Figure 5 shows worse scaled-prior TICA-W2 at 800 K, unlike the uniformly favorable comparison in v1.

T1.justification: The center-of-mass likelihood adjustment changes the quadratic term's sign from negative in v1 Equation 12 to positive in v2 Equation 37, a non-equivalent mathematical revision. The temperature appendix also changes the stated Gaussian prior variance from 1/beta² to 1/beta. The principal flow and AIS derivations are otherwise retained or restated.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows fine-tuning performance from 'superior' to established methods on unseen tetrapeptides to 'competitive' performance. The central contributions—transferable all-atom normalizing flows, efficient likelihood evaluation, ManyPeptidesMD, and amortized sampling—remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies pretrained-baseline comparisons because their training distributions differ. Its conclusion replaces the inference that the proposal is 'very close' to the target with a coverage-based interpretation and qualifications about the simple SMC implementations tested. New ablation and scaling discussions reconsider conditioning, parameter allocation, and training-data requirements, substantially expanding the interpretation of when the approach works.

D1.justification: V2 documents tokenization, padding rules, the eight-block permutation sequence, branch/ring variants, and look-ahead conditioning in substantially greater detail. It specifies dimensions of parameter-matched controls and adds baseline adaptation procedures and code-access links for BioEmu and UniSim. Training hardware documentation is also revised. These are substantial reproducibility additions, not evidence that every newly described detail changed implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused positioning around Jing et al. (2022), acknowledging earlier torsional transferable Boltzmann generators and connecting self-improvement to their energy-based training. It also adds supporting references for emulators, SMC, architecture components, and new evaluations. The central positioning as a scalable all-atom transferable flow remains.

P1.justification: Background explanations, related work, conclusions, and experiment narration receive substantial rewriting. Experimental configuration and temperature transfer become separate subsections, while the appendices are extensively reordered to place architecture and sampling formulations before training, evaluation, and additional results. 'Self-refinement' is renamed 'self-improvement.'

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from four to six panels, and Tables 2–4 are expanded or restructured. V2 adds the permutation table, dataset-scaling figure, and several supplementary result tables. Existing architecture, self-improvement, Ramachandran, and temperature displays are relocated or redrawn, with changes to legends, colors, axes, and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of scalability through full-range ablations, octopeptide sampler comparisons, and tests of data requirements and extrapolation beyond training lengths. Expanded implementation details address important reproducibility gaps, while the abstract moderates the fine-tuning claim. Mismatched pretrained baselines limit some comparisons, and Figure 5 still contradicts the claim of universally better temperature transfer at 800 K on TICA-W2. Nevertheless, the stronger validation and greater transparency provide a substantial net improvement.
